lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02 panel 2

measurements.source_note: layout.json has no scorecard 'elements' array; measured from its DOM boxes (CSS px, 1 px = 0.2646 mm) plus the 2550x3300 render

margins_text_safe.verdict: FAIL: the top margin is double the others (the declared margins are not equal within 1 mm). The top-left 126 px band above the wordmark is empty cream with no job

left_edges.note: The 6 px offset is optical sidebearing on the C; it reads as aligned. PASS

headers.verdict: PASS, but the H2s (10.9 pt) are smaller than the item names (12.75 pt). Colour and tracking alone carry that level

measurements.baseline_grid: None declared. Row pitches of 51.9, 33.4, 33 and 42 px share no module; Beer (686.8) and Spirits (634.8) do not line up across the columns

contrast_worst_pixel.verdict: PASS. The terracotta heads have only 0.49 of headroom under warm bar light

price_pair_scan_pct_of_300px_column.verdict: FAIL: fix_remote_prices. The price track was sized for the longest name (Brown Butter Old Fashioned), so every short name floats. The claim of a 'short hop' in proposal.md is false

measurements.dead_space: There is a 33 mm empty band above CANTINA on the left, a 79 px gap between the sub-line and the columns, and a thin right column where the three Spirits rows have no descriptions
measurements.content_check: 3 of 14 items have no description element (Blanco Tequila, Anejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP). The cocktail lines name a spirit plus at least 2 other ingredients: PASS

remove: The 'GOOD DRINKS / GOOD PEOPLE' tagline stack is lifted verbatim from the reference boards and says nothing about this venue or Iowa City. It is filler that props up a corner and is not a signature.
top_problem: This is ref-02 panel 2 traced and emptied. The sun disc, the stair, CANTINA, the cream ground, the two short columns and the tagline stack are all copied, and the painterly agave, the dark arch and the paper materiality that made the reference sing have been removed. The 'Iowa contour terraces' thesis is invisible: Iowa terraces are curved contours, and a six-step block reads as a generic stair. Cinzel's Roman inscriptional capitals say Tuscan wine bar, not a Mexican cantina. The single boldest missing idea is one ownable gesture that fuses the two places, for example the stepped Mesoamerican greca/step-fret and Iowa's curved contour furrows drawn as one continuous single-weight line system that also carries the section rhythm, so the art organises the menu instead of sitting in two corners.
fixes: Cut the price track from 238 px to the median name length plus 3 em (about 150 px, putting prices about 15 px after typical names), or set prices inline one en-space after each name, so every row stays under 30% eye travel on both print and phone and clears menu_item_association.

Equalise the text safe area: raise the wordmark group so the top inset matches the 16.5 mm left, right and bottom insets, or give that top band a job (let the disc and wordmark collision occupy it), and hang the reading layer on one baseline module (for example 13 px) so both columns share row lines.

Replace the borrowed stair with one legible gesture that does the thesis's work: curved contour furrows that echo a step-fret (one stroke weight, one ink), cropped with intent and connected to the disc so sun and land read as one horizon rather than two corner stamps.

Swap Cinzel for a display face with Mexican vernacular roots (a rotulo-derived grotesk or a condensed Latin sans, used as structure rather than costume), and push the knock-out collision further so the wordmark and sun are unmistakably one mark.

Give the section heads real rank (about 13-14 pt, or item size with heavier tracking), add a quiet ink-2 type line under the Spirits rows (blanco/añejo/VSOP facts from the draft only) so the right column carries the same row grid as the left, and add a restrained paper or print materiality (a flat ink misregistration or an uncoated-stock tone), justified by the thesis, so the page stops reading as default vector output.

lens: Items and prices vs draft_doc.json (revision 3), ingredient names and how complete the descriptions are (with meta.public_components), section flow for an Iowa City Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar
top_problem: A clean frame around content that is too thin. Three spirits have no description at all. The beer, rosé and cider lines were cut down to single words ('Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling', 'Dry sparkling'), and none of them gives beer style + ABV, wine grape + region or spirit age. The missing facts are not flagged as missing_ingredients. On top of that, short names sit about 60-70% of the column away from prices at the far right, with no leader or row rule.
problems: Prices: all 14 items and prices match the draft exactly (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Dry Cider 8). Nothing is invented and no item is dropped.

menu_item_association fails the measured price-pair scan. The price track is 214 px from the name start in a 238 px measure. Short names leave 150-215 px of empty travel to the price: Malbec→12, Dry Cider→8, Amber Lager→7, Czech Pilsner→7 and Pinot Grigio→11 are all about 55-70% of the column. There is no leader or row rule, and the track is sized for 'Brown Butter Old Fashioned' alone.

Spirits: Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print no description line, so the rule that every item has a description fails. Their age and type ride only on the name, and the missing facts (agave source, age, region) are not flagged as missing_ingredients.

Beer: no ABV and no style on two of three items. 'Toasty' (Amber Lager) and 'Hop-forward' (IPA) are adjectives, not styles. The draft had 'Toasty amber lager' and 'Hop-forward draft IPA', and the edit that removed the echo also removed the only style word. The proposal notes the ABV gap nowhere.
Wine: 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' give neither the region nor the producer. Brut Rosé was cut to 'Dry sparkling', which drops 'rosé', the only colour/style cue. No missing_ingredients flag.
Cider: 'Sparkling' alone. The apple and producer are unknown and not flagged.

Cocktails: none of the four prints a garnish except Manhattan (cocktail cherry). Margarita, Daiquiri and Old Fashioned garnishes are neither shown nor flagged as unknown. Aromatic bitters are correctly hidden on the Manhattan per public_components (the draft's own desc still says 'aromatic bitters'; that conflict should go to the Coordinator). The Margarita's second sentence was dropped; this is noted in the proposal and is acceptable.
Flow: Cider is stranded last, after Spirits. By style it belongs with Beer, straight after Draft, not after the Cognac pour.

Venue fit and flow: this is a Mexican cantina, yet the 'Agave' sub head was deleted and the two tequilas are merged into generic 'Spirits' beside Cognac. The one category the venue should own gets the least presence on the page. The Margarita is listed second under 'Classics', behind a Manhattan.
Structure change without owner sign-off: the draft sub heads 'Agave' and 'Brandy' were removed. It is noted in the subtraction log but is still an edit to the draft structure.

Coherence: the naming voice is inconsistent. The Margarita line says 'Tequila blanco' but the item is 'Blanco Tequila'. The Daiquiri says 'house demerara syrup' but the Old Fashioned says 'demerara'. Full ingredient lines in Cocktails sit beside one-word lines elsewhere, so the sections read as written at different levels of care.
Taglines: 'Good drinks / Good people' and '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' are generic brand or venue voice with no item fact. They pass.
fixes: Pull the price track in to about 8-12 px after each name, or add a dotted leader or thin row rule on every row, so no row goes over ~40% eye travel; this clears the menu_item_association gate.

Restore the draft's style words (e.g. 'Toasty amber lager', 'Hop-forward IPA', 'Dry sparkling rosé') and add flagged missing_ingredients placeholders for beer ABV, wine region/producer, cider apple/producer and spirit age/producer instead of printing nothing or one adjective.

Give each spirit a description line from known facts (e.g. 'Unaged tequila', 'Aged tequila', 'VSOP-grade Cognac'), confirm them with the Coordinator, and restore the 'Agave' and 'Brandy' sub heads so the cantina's agave list is named and grouped.
Move Cider directly under Beer (Cocktails → Beer → Cider → Wine → Spirits) so the lower-ABV pours read together and Spirits closes the list.

Standardise ingredient wording across cocktails (e.g. 'blanco tequila' to match the item name, 'demerara syrup' on both demerara drinks), and flag missing garnishes for the Margarita, Daiquiri and Old Fashioned rather than leaving them out silently.

lens: Traced every printed ingredient and label to build/draft_doc.json (rev 3) and to phg.menu_items / phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b (gateway log_id 211). Checked how descriptions and prices sit together in explore-H/preview-letter.png, including the price-to-item gate.
top_problem: Most rows fail the price-pair scan and nothing ties the price back to its name. Prices are right-aligned at x≈302 px in a 238 px name track, and the avoid-list bans leaders and row rules. Eye travel as a share of the 300 px column is about 46% for Manhattan (name ends ≈139 px, price ≈278 px), about 55% for Malbec (≈500 to ≈667 px), about 50% for Dry Cider, and about 45% each for Czech Pilsner, Amber Lager and Pinot Grigio. Every one of those is over the 40% limit, so menu_item_association fails under scorecard 1a. Layout problems on top of that: (a) the Brown Butter Old Fashioned description runs to ≈311 px, past the price column's right edge at ≈302 px, so its '16' sits inside the description's measure. (b) Brut Rosé has no serve label: it sits under SPARKLING, not BY THE GLASS, so a 13 could be glass or bottle. (c) The draft's only serve fact for spirits is 'pour' (draft desc 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'), and it is dropped, so 12 / 16 / 18 have no pour label. Accuracy of the facts that are printed is clean. Manhattan 'Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · cocktail cherry' matches the draft components Rye Whiskey / Sweet Vermouth / Cocktail Cherry and recipe_versions 9fb77eaa garnish 'Cocktail cherry'. Aromatic Bitters is correctly hidden (public_components.aromatic-bitters=false). Margarita, House Daiquiri and Brown Butter Old Fashioned are the draft's desc text with commas changed to middots. The beer, wine and cider stubs are deletions from the draft desc ('Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Dry sparkling rosé.', 'Dry sparkling cider.'). Añejo keeps its tilde. Every price matches menu_items.menu_price. The tagline 'Good drinks / Good people' is generic and states no item fact. Minor notes: (1) the draft doc has no venue-name field (title 'Bar menu'), so the CANTINA wordmark is taken from the brief, not from data. (2) The database also holds a 'Junmai Ginjo' item at 12 that is not in draft rev 3; that is a draft-sync issue, not a design issue. Description quality (12): the cocktails are bare ingredient lists, and the draft's one sensory phrase ('Bright and citrus-forward', Margarita) was deleted. Beer, wine and cider are cut down to one-word stubs ('Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling'). 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' are category wording. Spirits get nothing. That is two voices, and neither is appetising. Venue fit (13): for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in ZIP 52240, the census row (phg_census_zcta) gives median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, median household income $52,960 and 11% Hispanic/Latino. Yet the design deletes the draft's only agave cue (the 'Agave' sub head under Spirits, draft sub id sub_spirits_agave), leads with a Manhattan rather than the Margarita, and uses no Spanish beyond the product words blanco and añejo. The tequilas sit mid-column-two with the same weight as Cognac. The sun and terrace abstraction reads 'Southwest' more than 'cantina'. $14-16 cocktails are at the top of the tier for a college-town median income.
fixes: Fix the association gate without breaking the thesis. Set the price inline, one em after the name (for example 'Manhattan  15', same baseline), or shrink the name track to about 150 px so no row's eye travel is over 40%. Or add a hairline dotted leader, and move 'leaders' off the avoid-list; that is a note for the designer.

Put the serve labels back from the draft: 'pour' for the spirits (draft desc 'Blanco tequila pour.' etc., or a SPIRITS sub head such as 'por copa / pour'), and a glass label on Brut Rosé (move it under BY THE GLASS or add 'glass'). No 13, 12, 16 or 18 should be left for the guest to interpret.

Restore the draft's 'Agave' sub head (with 'Brandy', or just Agave above Cognac) and consider leading Classics with the Margarita. The tequila list is this venue's identity, and the draft already carries it.

Rewrite the stub descriptions in guest language, using only draft facts. Keep 'Bright and citrus-forward' on the Margarita. Use 'Crisp, hop-forward' for the IPA and 'Dry and sparkling' for the Cider, not one-word stubs. Replace the 'Dry red wine' / 'Dry white wine' category wording, and flag missing_ingredients (grape origin/region for the wines, style/ABV for the beers) instead of printing class names.

Cap the description measure at the price column's right edge (≈302 px). The Brown Butter Old Fashioned line currently runs to ≈311 px under its own price. Either wrap it or use the draft desc's shorter 'Brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara · bitters' at a narrower track so the price sits clear.
